description: The bar chart, titled "Dataset Statistics" and associated with the paper "EssayBench Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing," displays the sample counts for four different essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—across two distinct types of writing tasks: Open-ended (labeled "Open") and constrained (labeled "Cons."). The vertical y-axis represents the "Sample Count," ranging from 0 to 120 in increments of 20. The horizontal x-axis lists the four genres. For each genre, two bars are shown: a light blue bar for the Open set and a light pink bar for the Cons. set. The specific sample counts are as follows: for Argumentative, 79 (Open) and 122 (Cons.); for Narrative, 80 (Open) and 87 (Cons.); for Descriptive, 68 (Open) and 100 (Cons.); and for Expository, 62 (Open) and 130 (Cons.). The chart clearly illustrates that for all four genres, the constrained set has a higher sample count than the open-ended set. The tallest bar is the "Cons." bar for Expository, with a count of 130, while the shortest is the "Open" bar for Expository, with a count of 62.
